outcome: HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets)
cohort: The study included 7986 women with singleton births between 22-43 weeks' gestation recorded in a tertiary-level hospital birth register in Johannesburg, South Africa, from July 2017 to June 2018.
finding: High temperatures in early pregnancy (specifically weeks 3 and 4) were associated with an increased risk of pre-eclampsia/eclampsia/HELLP, while low temperatures during the third trimester were associated with an increased risk of high blood pressure/hypertension/gestational hypertension.
